content.content:
# Resend — transactional email for Next.js Resend sends an app's transactional email (welcome emails, password resets, receipts) through a small HTTP API with delivery logs, webhooks and domain verification. The official Node.js library `resend` wraps the whole Resend REST API, has typed responses and works in Node.js 18+, serverless and edge runtimes. ## Install ```bash npm install resend ``` ## 1. Environment variables `.env.local`: ``` RESEND_API_KEY=re_placeholder RESEND_FROM_EMAIL=hello@example.com ``` The API key is created in the Resend dashboard (API Keys). The From address must be on a domain you have verified in Resend, or `onboarding@resend.dev` while testing. ## 2. Create a client `src/lib/resend.ts`: ```ts import { Resend } from "resend"; export const resend = new Resend(process.env.RESEND_API_KEY!); ``` Use the client only in server code (route handlers, server actions, server components). Never expose the API key to the browser. ## 3. Send an email ```ts import { resend } from "@/lib/resend"; const { data, error } = await resend.emails.send({ from: process.env.RESEND_FROM_EMAIL!, to: "user@example.com", subject: "Welcome!", html: "

Thanks for signing up.

", text: "Thanks for signing up.", }); ``` `data.id` is the message id; use it to look the email up in the dashboard logs. ## 4. Send with a React template Write the email as a React component and pass it with `react`; Resend renders it to HTML: ```tsx import { resend } from "@/lib/resend"; import { PasswordResetEmail } from "@/emails/password-reset"; await resend.emails.send({ from: process.env.RESEND_FROM_EMAIL!, to: "user@example.com", subject: "Reset your password", react: PasswordResetEmail({ name: "Ada", actionUrl: "https://example.com/reset?token=..." }), }); ``` The `@react-email/components` package gives layout primitives for email clients; plain JSX works too. ## 5. Handle errors `emails.send` does not throw on a refused message: it resolves to `{ data: null, error }` with the error `name` and `message` from Resend (invalid API key, unverified domain, rate limit). Check `error` where the email is triggered so a failed email does not break the request that caused it. ## Why teams pick Resend - Built for developers: one API call to send, typed SDK, React templates in the codebase. - Delivery logs, bounces and webhooks live in the same dashboard as the API keys. - Domain verification with DKIM and SPF guided from the dashboard. # Notely A small team notes app. Next.js App Router + TypeScript + Tailwind. ## Status - Users live in `src/lib/users.ts` as an in-memory list. - `/dashboard` shows the current user and the team. - There is no sign-in, no billing, and no email yet. ## Develop ```bash npm run dev ``` dashboard favicon.ico globals.css layout.tsx page.tsx

content.text:
Notely now sends a welcome email when a user is created and a password reset email when a reset is requested, both through Resend. I haven't sent a real email, because the credentials are placeholders. Lint passes. `tsc` reports one error in `src/app/layout.tsx` (`LayoutProps` not found), a file this change doesn't touch. I didn't check whether it was already failing before my changes.

I chose Resend because the repo already had its docs, and it has a small typed SDK. I wrote the emails as plain HTML and text strings, so the only new dependency is `resend`.

- **`src/lib/email.ts`** (new):
  - It holds the Resend client, a `sendWelcomeEmail` function and a `sendPasswordResetEmail` function. Names in the HTML are escaped.
  - A failed send is logged and swallowed, so it can't break the request that triggered it. Resend returns errors instead of throwing, and the helper handles both cases.
- **`src/lib/users.ts`:**
  - **`createUser`:** this didn't exist, so I added it. It lowercases the email and rejects duplicates. It adds the user to the in-memory list, then sends the welcome email.
  - **`requestPasswordReset(email)`:** it creates a random token that expires after 1 hour and emails a link to `/reset-password?token=…`. Only a hash of the token is stored. It does nothing for an unknown email, so callers can't tell whether an address is registered.
  - **`consumePasswordResetToken(token)`:** this is single-use. It returns the user the token belongs to, or `undefined` if the token is invalid or expired.
- **`.env.example`:** it has `RESEND_API_KEY`, `RESEND_FROM_EMAIL` and `APP_URL`, all placeholders. `.gitignore` was ignoring every `.env*` file, so I added an exception for `.env.example`.
- **`README.md`:** the status line now mentions the email setup.

There is no `/reset-password` page yet, so the link in the reset email leads nowhere. There is also no sign-up form or API route calling `createUser`. The app has no sign-in or password storage to attach them to, so I left those out.
